examples.en: My younger sister became a middle school girl this year.

examples.ko: 버스에서 여중생 두 명이 웃고 있었어요.
examples.en: Two middle school girls were laughing on the bus.
That middle school girl is very good at running.
The middle school girls lined up in their uniforms.
My teacher does the work of teaching middle school girls.

examples.ko: 여중생에게 인기 있는 책을 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: Please recommend a book that is popular with middle school girls.

explain: '여자 중학생'을 줄인 말이에요. '여-'는 여자라는 뜻이라서 '여고생', '여대생'도 같은 방식이에요. 남자는 '남중생'이라고도 하고, 성별을 따지지 않으면 '중학생'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저기 있는 여자 중학생이 제 동생이에요.
phrases.en: That middle school girl over there is my younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이지 않은 원래 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full, unshortened form.

phrases.en: The middle school girls are laughing in front of the school gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 명을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '들' to talk about more than one.

phrases.example: 교실에 여중생 한 명이 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: One middle school girl is still in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람은 '명'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: People are counted with '명'.

explain_en: It is a shortened form of '여자 중학생'. The '여-' means female, so '여고생' and '여대생' work the same way. For boys people also say '남중생', and if gender does not matter, '중학생'.

examples.en: I study English literature at university.
We read Shakespeare in English literature class.
My older sister graduated from the English literature department and became a translator.
I borrowed a book about English literature from the library.
English literature is fun too, but I like Korean literature more.

examples.ko: 영문학이 어렵다는 친구도 있고 쉽다는 친구도 있어요.
examples.en: Some friends say English literature is hard and others say it is easy.

explain: 대학교 전공 이름으로 써요. 나라 이름을 줄여 '문학'을 붙이는 방식은 '국문학'(한국 문학), '불문학'(프랑스 문학)에도 보여요. 전공 학과는 '영문학과'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is in the English literature department.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영문학'은 공부하는 분야이고 '영문학과'는 대학교의 학과 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 영문학 is the field; 영문학과 is the university department.

phrases.en: I majored in English literature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교에서 무엇을 공부했는지 말할 때 '전공하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 전공하다 to say what you majored in.

phrases.en: Today's English literature class was fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교에서 듣는 수업을 말할 때 '수업'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 수업 refers to a class in the subject.

explain_en: It is used as a university major. Abbreviating the country name and adding '문학' also appears in '국문학' (Korean literature) and '불문학' (French literature). The department is '영문학과'.

examples.en: Our school holds a field day in autumn.
The field day was postponed because of rain.
I came first in the race at the field day.
On field day we bring gimbap.
The parents also took part in their child's field day.
I like May, when we have field day and go on picnics.

explain: 학교에서 달리기, 줄다리기 같은 경기를 하는 행사예요. 청군과 백군으로 팀을 나누기도 해요. 대학교나 회사의 큰 행사는 '체육대회'라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 가을 운동회에서 우리 반이 줄다리기를 이겼어요.
phrases.en: Our class won the tug of war at the fall field day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 학교에서는 보통 가을이나 봄에 운동회를 해요. 계절을 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Korean schools usually hold field days in fall or spring; the season goes in front.

phrases.en: On field day, we bring a packed lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동회를 하는 바로 그날을 말해요. 날씨 이야기를 할 때도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The very day the field day takes place; often used when talking about the weather.

phrases.en: My company is holding an athletic meet next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동회와 비슷하지만 대학교나 회사의 큰 행사에 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 운동회, but used more for big events at universities or companies.

explain_en: It is a school event with games like races and tug-of-war, sometimes split into blue and white teams. A large event at a university or company may be called '체육대회'.

en: student preparing for an entrance exam

examples.en: Exam-prep students go to cram school even during vacation.
Last year I was an entrance-exam student.

examples.ko: 입시생 자녀를 둔 부모님은 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: Parents with a child preparing for entrance exams worry a lot.
The library is full of students preparing for exams.

examples.ko: 입시생에게는 마지막 한 달이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: For exam-prep students the final month is the most important.

examples.ko: 입시생을 위한 간식 세트를 팔고 있어요.
examples.en: They're selling snack sets for students preparing for exams.

explain: 대학 입시를 준비하는 학생을 말해요. '수험생'은 입시뿐 아니라 자격시험 등 다른 시험을 준비하는 사람까지 넓게 가리켜요. 입시를 한 번 더 준비하는 사람은 '재수생'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm an exam-prep student now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신이 입시를 준비하는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you're preparing for the entrance exam.

phrases.en: I bought a cheering gift for the exam takers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 준비하는 사람을 더 넓게 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers more broadly to anyone preparing for exams.

phrases.en: My older brother is retaking the entrance exam this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입시를 한 번 더 준비하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Someone preparing for the exam one more time.

explain_en: It refers to a student preparing for university entrance exams. '수험생' is broader and includes people preparing for any exam, such as certifications. Someone retaking the entrance exam is called a '재수생'.

examples.ko: 서점에서 수학 참고서를 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a math reference book at the bookstore.
I marked the parts I did not understand in the study guide.
I inherited the study guide my older brother used.
This study guide is good because the explanations are easy.
Please use the textbook and the study guide together.
I have so many study guides that my bag is heavy.

explain: 학교에서 쓰는 '교과서'를 보충해 주는 공부 책이에요. 문제를 많이 푸는 책은 보통 '문제집'이라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.en: I bought an English study guide and study with it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과목 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 참고서인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a subject name first to say which study guide.

phrases.en: For problems I don't know, I check the study guide and solve them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모르는 것을 찾아볼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking things up.
phrases.en_equiv: to look at a study guide

phrases.example: 참고서 말고 문제집도 한 권 샀어요.
phrases.en: Besides the study guide, I also bought a workbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 많이 풀어 보는 책이라 참고서와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: A book of practice problems, different from a study guide.

explain_en: It is a study book that supplements the school '교과서' (textbook). A book mainly full of practice problems is usually called a '문제집' instead.

examples.en: I am studying Korean studies at university.
The Korean studies class is really fun.

examples.ko: 한국학은 역사와 문화를 함께 배우는 학문이에요.
examples.en: Korean studies is a field where you learn history and culture together.

examples.ko: 한국학에 관심이 많은 외국 학생이 늘었어요.
examples.en: There are more foreign students interested in Korean studies.

examples.ko: 한국학도 이제 전 세계에서 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can now study Korean studies all over the world.
Our university has newly opened a Korean studies department.

explain: '-학'은 학문 이름에 붙어요. 한국학, 중국학, 일본학처럼 한 나라를 연구하는 학문에 써요. 한국어 자체를 연구하는 분야는 '한국어학'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I want to enter the Korean studies department.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교에서 한국학을 가르치는 학과 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a university department that teaches Korean studies.

phrases.en: I majored in Korean studies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교에서 주로 공부한 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what you mainly studied at university.

phrases.en: I read a book written by a Korean studies scholar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-자'를 붙여 한국학을 연구하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-자' makes it a person who studies Korean studies.

explain_en: The ending '-학' marks a field of study, as in 한국학, 중국학, and 일본학. The study of the Korean language itself is called '한국어학'.

examples.en: I sprayed hairspray on my hair.
This spray smells nice.
I painted a picture on the wall with spray paint.
There is a mosquito spray in my bag.
The tip of the spray is clogged, so nothing comes out.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 작은 스프레이도 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed a small spray bottle for the trip too.

explain: 분무기처럼 뿜어 나오는 액체 전체에 써요. 머리에 쓰면 '헤어스프레이', 벌레를 쫓으면 '모기 스프레이'처럼 쓰임을 앞에 붙여서 불러요. 뿌릴 때는 '뿌리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I spray my hair before going out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스프레이'와 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb used with 스프레이.

phrases.en: I went to the store to buy hairspray.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리 모양을 고정하는 스프레이를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the spray used to hold a hairstyle.

phrases.en: I spray mosquito spray at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레를 쫓는 스프레이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the spray that keeps insects away.

explain_en: It covers any liquid that comes out in a mist. The use goes in front: 헤어스프레이 for hair, 모기 스프레이 for keeping mosquitoes away. To spray it, use 뿌리다.

examples.en: I let the steam out of the pressure cooker and opened the lid.

examples.ko: 압력솥으로 밥을 하면 훨씬 빨리 돼요.
examples.en: Cooking rice in a pressure cooker is much faster.
The pressure cooker started making a hissing sound.
If you make braised ribs in a pressure cooker, the meat gets tender.
My mother boiled potatoes in the pressure cooker.

examples.ko: 압력솥 뚜껑이 안 열려서 한참 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The pressure cooker lid wouldn't open, so I waited a long time.

explain: '밥솥'은 밥을 짓는 솥이고, '압력솥'은 압력으로 음식을 빨리 익히는 솥이라 찜이나 삶는 요리에도 써요. '김'은 뜨거운 수증기를 뜻해서 '김이 나다', '김을 빼다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 압력솥에 밥을 하면 더 맛있어요.
phrases.en: Rice tastes better when I cook it in a pressure cooker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 빨리 하면서 맛있게 짓는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes cooking rice quickly and deliciously.
phrases.en_equiv: to cook rice in a pressure cooker

phrases.en: I boiled a chicken in the pressure cooker and it cooked quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 걸리는 요리를 빨리 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for dishes that normally take a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: to boil in a pressure cooker

phrases.en: You must close the pressure cooker lid tightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용할 때 조심해야 하는 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a part you need to be careful with when using it.

explain_en: A '밥솥' is a pot for cooking rice, while a '압력솥' cooks food quickly under pressure, so it is also used for braising and boiling. Here '김' means hot steam, as in '김이 나다' (steam comes out) and '김을 빼다' (let the steam out).

examples.en: The children are playing ball in the front yard.
There is a persimmon tree in the front yard of my grandmother's house.
When spring comes, we plant flowers in the front yard.
I feel refreshed after sweeping the front yard.
The puppy runs around happily in the front yard.
We made a small vegetable patch in the front yard of our house.

explain: 집 앞쪽에 있는 뜰이고, 반대말은 '뒤뜰'이에요. 단독 주택이나 시골집 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 일반적으로 집 앞 공간은 '마당'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 우리 집 마당에는 작은 꽃밭이 있어요.
phrases.en: Our yard has a small flower bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 앞이나 집 안에 있는 넓은 빈터를 두루 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general word for the open space around a house, in front or inside the grounds.

phrases.en: I planted flowers in the front yard in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 앞 정원을 가꾸는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes tending a garden in front of the house.
phrases.en_equiv: to plant flowers in the front yard

phrases.example: 그 집은 앞뜰이 넓어서 강아지가 뛰어놀기 좋아요.
phrases.en: That house has a big front yard, so it's good for a dog to run around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜰의 크기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the size of the yard.

explain_en: It is the garden in front of a house, and the opposite is '뒤뜰' (backyard). It mostly appears when talking about detached houses or country homes, and the open space in front of a house is also generally called '마당'.

examples.en: I recycled old clothes into a bag.
Plastic can only be recycled if you sort it.
This paper cup is hard to recycle.
Don't throw the bottle away; try reusing it.
Our shop reuses packaging boxes.
The souvenir is a bag made of recycled fabric.

explain: '재활용품', '재활용 쓰레기', '재활용 센터'처럼 앞말로도 많이 써요. 쓰레기를 종류별로 나눠 버리는 건 '분리수거'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '다시 쓰다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I collected the recyclables and put them out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 쓸 수 있는 물건을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for things that can be used again.

phrases.en: Glass bottles can be recycled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 물건이 재활용되는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say which things can be recycled.

phrases.en: I collect used paper and use it again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '재활용하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday phrase used instead of '재활용하다'.

explain_en: It is often used before another noun, as in '재활용품', '재활용 쓰레기' and '재활용 센터'. Sorting trash by type is called '분리수거'. In daily talk people also say '다시 쓰다'.

examples.en: I listen to music with headphones on the subway.

examples.ko: 새 헤드폰을 사고 싶어서 가격을 비교하고 있어요.
examples.en: I want to buy new headphones, so I am comparing prices.
The headphones fit tightly on my ears and hurt.
I put my headphones in my bag so I do not lose them.

examples.ko: 이 헤드폰 정말 가볍고 소리도 선명해요.
examples.en: These headphones are really light and the sound is clear.
I made a call with the microphone on the headphones.

explain: '이어폰'은 귀에 꽂고 헤드폰은 머리에 걸쳐요. 헤드폰은 '끼다'와 '쓰다'를 모두 써요.

phrases.en: I wear headphones when I study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리나 귀에 걸쳐 착용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for putting them on over the head or ears.

phrases.en: At night I watch movies with headphones on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끼다'와 뜻이 같고 머리에 얹는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '끼다', with a feeling of putting it on the head.

phrases.en: They are wireless headphones, so they are convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선이 없는 헤드폰을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Headphones without a cable.

explain_en: 이어폰 goes into your ears, while 헤드폰 sits over your head. For wearing headphones, both 끼다 and 쓰다 are used.

examples.ko: 학원 등록비가 한 달에 십만 원이에요.
examples.en: The academy's registration fee is 100,000 won a month.
You have to pay the registration fee when you apply.
I paid the swimming pool registration fee by card.
This year the registration fee went up compared to last year.
The textbook cost is also included in the registration fee.

examples.ko: 이미 낸 등록비를 돌려받을 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can I get back the registration fee I already paid?

explain: 학원, 운동 시설, 동호회 같은 곳에 처음 등록할 때 내는 돈이에요. 대학교에서 내는 돈은 보통 '등록금'이라고 해요. 매달 내는 돈은 '수강료'나 '회비'처럼 따로 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I went to the gym today and paid the registration fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내다'와 함께 돈을 지불하는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for paying the fee, with 내다.

phrases.en: The registration fee at this swimming pool is a bit expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '이/가'와 형용사를 붙여 값이 어떤지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the subject particle with an adjective to describe the price.

phrases.en: How much is the registration fee for this club?
phrases.nuance_ko: 등록하기 전에 가격을 물어볼 때 쓰는 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A question for asking the price before signing up.

explain_en: It is the money you pay when first signing up for places like academies, gyms or clubs. What students pay at a university is usually called '등록금'. Monthly payments are often called '수강료' or '회비'.

examples.en: I volunteer at a nursing home every weekend.
In college, I volunteered abroad every vacation.
There are many people who volunteer for their neighbors.

examples.ko: 내일 같이 봉사할 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone to volunteer with tomorrow.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 책을 읽어 주며 봉사하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to volunteer by reading books to children.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어도 사회에 봉사하면서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: Even when I'm older, I want to live serving society.

explain: 돈을 받지 않고 남을 돕는 일에 주로 써요. 보통 '봉사 활동을 하다'라고 말하고, 가게에서 손님을 대하는 일은 '서비스'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 한 달에 한 번 봉사 활동을 해요.
phrases.en: I do volunteer work once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '봉사하다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More commonly used than the verb 봉사하다 itself.

phrases.en: On weekends, I volunteer at a hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 원해서 돈을 받지 않고 돕는 일이라는 뜻이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes it clear you help by your own choice without pay.

phrases.en: This Saturday I am going to volunteer with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봉사하려고 어디에 간다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are going somewhere in order to volunteer.

explain_en: It mostly refers to helping others without pay, and people often say '봉사 활동을 하다'. Treating customers in a shop is called '서비스' instead.

t90.ax: I volunteer at a nursing home every weekend.

examples.ko: 저는 열 살 때 새어머니를 만났어요.
examples.en: I met my stepmother when I was ten.
My stepmother cares for me like her own daughter.
My stepmother made me a delicious kimchi stew.
At first, talking with my stepmother felt awkward.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 새어머니가 나쁜 사람으로 나올 때가 많아요.
examples.en: In dramas, the stepmother is often shown as a bad person.
On Parents' Day this time, I gave flowers to my stepmother.

explain: '계모'라는 말도 있지만 부정적인 느낌이 강해서, 말할 때나 부를 때는 '새어머니'가 부드러워요. 아버지 쪽은 '새아버지'라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '어머니'나 '엄마'라고 많이 불러요.

phrases.en: My stepmom takes really good care of me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새어머니'보다 편하고 친근한 말이고, 부를 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual and friendly word than '새어머니', and it can also be used to address her.

phrases.en: My stepmother packed a lunch for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높여서 말할 때 '께서'와 '-시-'를 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '께서' and '-시-' together to show respect when talking about her.

phrases.en: I live with my father and my stepmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족 이야기를 할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about your family.

explain_en: There is also the word '계모', but it carries a strong negative feeling, so '새어머니' is gentler when talking about her. The father's side is '새아버지'. When addressing her directly, people often just say '어머니' or '엄마'.

t90.ax: I met my stepmother when I was ten.
